sources.entry: motion.tools (Antragsgrün) - Manage motions and amendments for (political) conventions. (Demo, Source Code) AGPL-3.0 PHP/Docker

summary.one_liner: Antragsgrün (motion.tools) is a self-hostable PHP web tool for NGOs and political parties to draft, submit, amend, and vote on motions and resolutions.
summary.what_it_does: Antragsgrün lets organisations collect motions, proposals and discussion papers online, run a structured amendment process, and draft resolutions collaboratively. It also supports online votings, speaking lists, and a "currently debated" widget for meetings. Motions and amendments can hold content in several languages, and readers get a language picker with fallback notices. Export options include PDF generation via TCPDF by default, with optional Weasyprint rendering. The README also covers a REST API with OpenAPI docs, Redis caching, OpenTelemetry, optional background jobs, 2FA and CAPTCHA for accounts, and a plugin system for themes and language variants.
use_cases: Collect and discuss motions for a party convention
Run an amendment process for resolutions
Organize online votings during a meeting
Manage speaking lists at a conference
Export motions and amendments to PDF
how_to_run: Option A (pre-bundled): install PHP 8.2+ (8.4 recommended), MySQL/MariaDB, and Apache or nginx; extract the downloaded package into the web folder and use the web-based installer.
Then open the site to run the web installer; the bundled docker-compose.yml pre-configures MariaDB.
stack: RabbitMQ and Live Server (optional live updates)
notable: Multi-language content: motion and amendment text can be held in several languages at once, with fallback display for missing translations
Built-in accessibility goal of WCAG 2.0 AA and BITV2.0, with keyboard operation and Pa11y testing
Plugin architecture for custom themes, language variants, and automatic translation (a Claude API example is included)
Web-based installer and updater, plus per-user 2FA (TOTP) and configurable CAPTCHA for brute-force protection
Multisite mode and site manager for running many sites from one codebase
caveats: Requires a MySQL/MariaDB database and a PHP web server setup; the Docker path is the simplest route
Several features are optional and need separate setup: Weasyprint, ImageMagick, Redis, the RabbitMQ-based Live Server, and JWT keys
The README says the REST API does not yet cover all functionality and is still under development
